newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China invites Albright to HK handover --radio.
newsitem.headline: China invites Albright to HK handover --radio.

text.p: A Hong Kong politician said on Tuesday China's Foreign Minister Qian Qichen had invited U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to witness the colony's return to China by Britain, Hong Kong radio said.
Cheng Yiu-tong, a Hong Kong delegate to China's parliament, quoted Qian as saying he had extended the invitation when the two met in Beijing last week, the radio said.

This would make Albright the first foreign dignitary named by either Britain or China as a guest at the historic event, scheduled for midnight on June 30. Officially, London and Beijing have not agreed on a guest list.
Cheng attended a meeting in Beijing where Qian met Hong Kong deputies of the parliament, the National People's Congress.
Qian was quoted as saying he wanted to prove to Albright that accusations levelled against China by some people in Hong Kong were false.

He accused some people in the territory of fabricating charges that Beijing would be flouting the law by dissolving the territory's present legislature and repealing or amending some human rights laws, the radio said.
